units.text: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”
Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo prophesied a prophecy over the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, over them.
Then Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesous son of Iosedek arose and began building the house of God in Jerusalem. God’s prophets were with them, helping them.

The elders of the Jews and the Levites were building through the prophecy of Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo. They rebuilt and put it in order by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus, Darius and Arthasastha, kings of the Persians.
They completed this house by the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
“For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain

from the injustices of your fathers. You have turned aside from My ordinances and have not guarded them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord Almighty. And you said, “How shall we return?”
The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.
He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.
He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.
Comfort, comfort My people, says God.
You priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her. For her humiliation is fulfilled, her sin is loosed; for from the hand of the Lord she has received double for her sins.
A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; all the crooked places will become straight, and the rough country will become plains.
And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God; for the Lord has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry out!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as the flower of grass.
The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen;
but the word of our God remains for ever.
Because thus said the Lord: When seventy years are about to be fulfilled for Babylon, I will visit you and establish My words for you, to return your people to this place.
And I will plan for you a plan of peace and not evils, to give you these things.
And pray to Me, and I will listen to you.
And seek Me earnestly, and you will find Me, because you will seek Me with your whole heart,
and I will appear to you.
And all the land will become a ruin, and they will serve among the nations for seventy years.
And when the seventy years are fulfilled, I will exact justice from that nation, says the Lord, and make them an everlasting ruin.
“Sit stricken and enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will certainly no longer be called a kingdom’s strength.
I was provoked against My people; you defiled My inheritance. I gave it into your hand, but you gave them no mercy; you made the elder’s yoke exceedingly heavy.
You said, ‘I will rule for ever.’ You did not consider these things in your heart or remember the last things.
I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.
As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.
He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.
In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was captured, on that day the Lord’s hand came upon me, and He led me
in a vision of God into Israel’s land and set me upon a very high mountain. Upon it, opposite, was something like a city’s structure.
He brought me in there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like gleaming copper. In his hand were a builders’ cord and a measuring reed, and he stood at the gate.

The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

Behold, an enclosure surrounded the house outside. In the man’s hand was a reed measuring six cubits by the cubit and handbreadth. He measured the outer wall: its width equaled the reed, and its height equaled the reed.
But your grapes and fruit, mountains of Israel, My people will consume, for they are drawing near.
For behold, I am toward you; I will look upon you, and you will be cultivated and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, all Israel’s house completely. The cities will be inhabited and the devastated land rebuilt.
I will multiply humans and livestock upon you, settle you as at your beginning and do you good as in your former times. You will know that I am the Lord.
I will cause people, My people Israel, to be born upon you. They will inherit you, and you will be their possession. You certainly will no longer be bereaved of them.
because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
A song of the ascents. Those trusting in the Lord are like Mount Zion; the one dwelling in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Mountains are around her, and the Lord is around His people, from now and for ever.
For He will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous may not stretch out their hands in lawlessness.
